query: The 2022 Caillaud, Leveque, and Si-Tayeb STAR Protocols workflow for CRISPR-Cas9 RNP editing of human iPSCs with FACS single-cell sorting, including GPR146 deletion and IRX5 molecular-tag insertion examples, clonal culture, and genotyping
title: FACS-assisted CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing of human induced pluripotent stem cells
markdown:
## Protocol: The 2022 Caillaud, Leveque, and Si-Tayeb STAR Protocols workflow for CRISPR-Cas9 RNP editing of human iPSCs with FACS single-cell sorting, including GPR146 deletion and IRX5 molecular-tag insertion examples, clonal culture, and genotyping

### Overview

This protocol outlines the workflow for CRISPR-Cas9 ribonucleoprotein (RNP) editing of human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs), featuring FACS-based single-cell sorting, clonal culture, and genotyping. It includes specific examples for GPR146 deletion (knockout) and IRX5 molecular-tag insertion (knock-in). The process involves reagent preparation, hiPSC passaging and adaptation to single-cell dissociation, nucleofection with CRISPR-Cas9 tools, optional FACS sorting at 48 hours post-transfection, clonal expansion, and final genotyping or cryopreservation.

### Materials/Reagents

StemMACS iPS Brew XF Basal Medium; StemMACS iPS Brew XF 503 Supplement; Y27632 (10 mM stock); Alt-R CRISPR-Cas9 crRNA XT (200 mM); Alt-R CRISPR-Cas9 tracrRNA, ATTO 488 (200 mM); Alt-R S.p. HiFi Cas9 Nuclease V3 (61 mM); Opti-MEM; P3 Primary Cell Nucleofector Solution; Supplement 1 (Lonza P3 Primary Cell 4D Kit); Matrigel (human ESC qualified); Dulbecco's phosphate buffer solution without Ca2+/Mg2+ (DPBS wo Ca2+/Mg2+); Non-enzymatic gentle cell dissociation reagent (GCDR); DAPI solution (10 ng/mL final concentration); QuickExtract DNA extraction solution; CryoStor CS10 cryopreservation medium; BD FACSFlow; BD Cytometer Setup and Tracking (CS&T) beads; BD Accudrop beads.

### Equipment

BD FacsMelody cell sorter (or equivalent flow cytometry sorter capable of single-cell sorting in 96-well format); 4D-Nucleofector Core Unit with CA-137 program; 100 µL Nucleocuvette vessels (from P3 Primary Cell 4D Kit); 50 mL plastic tubes; 6-well cell culture plates; 96-well cell culture plates; 15 mL Falcon tubes; 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes; Malassez counting chamber; 70 µm nylon mesh cell strainer; 5 mL sterile polypropylene tubes suitable for cytometry; Thermocycler; Multichannel pipette; Inverted microscope.

### Safety & Sterility

Maintain aseptic conditions throughout all procedures, especially during FACS sorting and cell handling. Prepare two-part gRNAs under RNase-free conditions. Ensure hiPSCs are at very low passage and have recently checked for genomic integrity prior to editing. Maintain hypoxic conditions (4% O2, 5% CO2, 37°C) where specified to prevent spontaneous differentiation and maintain genetic stability. Keep FACS sorter sample chamber cooled to 4°C during sorting.

## Reagent Preparation

### Preparation

1. Prepare complete medium by adding StemMACS iPS Brew XF 503 Supplement to StemMACS iPSBrew XF Basal Medium. Mix well and prepare 40 mL aliquots in 50 mL plastic tubes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S01 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Store the prepared complete medium at 4°C for up to 2 weeks or freeze at -20°C for long-term storage. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S02 -->
2. Reagent Final concentration Amount

hiPSCs culturing medium N/A 40 mL

Y27632 (10 mM) 10 mM 40 mL

Prepare fresh medium to be used immediately or store it at 4 C for no longer than 4 days after preparation. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S03 -->
3. Complex the two-part gRNA by combining Alt-R CRISPR-Cas9 crRNA XT (200 mM) with ATTO 488 tracrRNA (200 mM) at equimolar concentrations (e.g., 3 mL of each to achieve a final 100 mM duplex). Heat the complex for 5 min at 95°C, then allow it to cool down on the bench. Store the crRNA XT:tracrRNA duplex at -20°C for several months if not used immediately. CRITICAL: Prepare the two-part gRNAs under RNase-free conditions. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S04 -->
4. Form the CRISPR-Cas9 RNP complex by mixing the crRNA XT:ATTO 488 tracrRNA duplex (100 mM) with Alt-R S.p. HiFi Cas9 Nuclease V3 (61 mM) in Opti-MEM. For one transfection reaction, mix 1.7 µL of duplex, 1.3 µL of Cas9 nuclease, and 2 µL Opti-MEM to achieve final concentrations of 34 mM duplex and 16 mM Cas9. Incubate the complex for 20 min at 21°C. CRITICAL: If two gRNAs are used for gene knockout, complex each gRNA independently with the HiFi Cas9 nuclease to avoid affinity competition. CRITICAL: Prepare the RNP complex fresh before transfection. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S05 -->
5. Dilute the single-strand oligo DNA donor with Opti-MEM to a final concentration of 1 mg/mL. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S06 -->
6. Prepare the transfection solution for the P3 Primary Cell 4D Kit following manufacturer instructions. For one transfection reaction using a 100 µL Nucleocuvette vessel, mix 82 µL P3 Primary Cell Nucleofector Solution with 18 µL Supplement 1. Prepare fresh and warm at 21°C for 20 min before use. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S07 -->

## Procedure

### Design and preparation of CRISPR-Cas9 tools

1. Design guide RNAs (gRNAs) using Integrated DNA Technologies (IDT) software or CRISPOR. Design a donor DNA sequence if performing gene knock-in (KI). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S01 -->

#### Branch A: Knockout (KO)

1. For Knockout (KO): Design two gRNAs targeting both sides of the genomic region to be deleted, as described in Xu et al. (2021). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S02 -->

#### Branch B: Knock-in (KI)

1. For Knock-in (KI): Design one gRNA and one donor DNA for single nucleotide mutation or molecular tag insertion. Ensure the gRNA cutting site is close to the insertion point (optimal bi-allelic insertion occurs when the cut site is within 10 bp of the target sequence, as described in Paquet et al. (2016)). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S03 -->

#### Shared continuation

> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL: hiPSCs used for CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing should be at very low passage and recently checked for genomic integrity. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S04 -->

### Passaging of hiPSCs

1. Perform hiPSC passaging in feeder-free conditions twice a week by dissociating cells into small aggregates for at least two weeks before transfection. Approximately three to five confluently growing wells of a 6-well plate are needed for one CRISPR experiment. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S01 -->
2. Prepare human embryonic stem cell (ESC) qualified Matrigel solution at 0.05 mg/mL. Coat each well of a 6-well plate with 1 mL Matrigel solution. Incubate the plate at 37°C for at least 1 h before cell passaging. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S02 -->
3. Monitor hiPSC confluency under an inverted microscope. Perform passaging when cells reach 70%-80% confluency. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S03 -->
4. Warm-up Dulbecco's phosphate buffer solution without Ca2+/Mg2+ (DPBS wo Ca2+/Mg2+), non-enzymatic gentle cell dissociation reagent (GCDR), and hiPSC culturing medium (e.g., StemMACS iPS Brew) at 21°C for at least 20 min before passaging. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S04 -->
5. Discard the old medium from the culture wells by aspiration. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S05 -->
6. Wash cells with 1 mL DPBS wo Ca2+/Mg2+ per well. Gently tap the plate to flush out dead cells, then aspirate the DPBS. Repeat this wash step twice. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S06 -->
7. Add 1 mL of GCDR to each well and incubate for 2-3 min at 21°C. Monitor hiPSC dissociation under an inverted microscope. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S07 -->
8. Discard the GCDR by aspiration as soon as cells start to dissociate from each other but before they fully detach from the plate. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S08 -->
9. Gently flush the dissociated hiPSC clusters from the well surface using 1 mL of pre-warmed culturing medium. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S09 -->
10. Adjust the final volume of the hiPSC suspension according to the total number of wells needed for replating. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S10 -->
11. Aspirate the Matrigel solution from the pre-coated 6-well plates. Pipet 1.5 mL of the hiPSC suspension into each well. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S11 -->
12. Grow cells at 37°C in a humidified atmosphere of 5% CO2 and 4% O2 to prevent spontaneous differentiation and maintain genetic stability. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S12 -->

### One day after passaging

1. One day after passaging, renew the medium with 1.5 mL fresh hiPSC culturing medium. Change the medium every two days thereafter. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T2-S01 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL: Adapting hiPSCs to small aggregate dissociation is a prerequisite for single-cell dissociation before hiPSC transfection and single-cell sorting. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T2-S02 -->

### FACS sorter set-up

1. Set up and perform calibration of the flow cytometry sorter instrument to ensure proper single-cell analysis and subsequent sorting in 96-well plate format. Use the steps below to calibrate the BD FacsMelody cell sorter. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S01 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL: Make sure that the FACS system is maintained under aseptic conditions. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S02 -->
2. Power ON the cytometer and connect annex instrumentation. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S03 -->
3. Refill the sheath fluid tank with BD FACSFlow and empty the waste tank whenever needed. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S04 -->
4. Perform instrument quality control using BD Cytometer Setup and Tracking (CS&T) beads to check system performance. Use BD Accudrop beads to set an accurate drop delay for cell sorting. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S05 -->
5. Cool down the sample chamber of the sorting system to 4°C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S06 -->
6. Define the desired experimental parameters on the sorter software. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S07 -->
7. Load an unstained control sample and adjust gates to identify single-cell populations as shown in Figure 3A. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S08 -->
8. Add DAPI solution (10 ng/mL final concentration) to the unstained control cells. Adjust gates to discriminate between dead cells (DAPI positive) and live cells (DAPI negative/unstained) as shown in Figure 3B. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S09 -->
9. Add DAPI solution (10 ng/mL final concentration) to the cells transfected with all CRISPR-Cas9 tools (refer to 'Transfection mixes' table in materials section). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S10 -->
10. Load the recipient 96-well plate into the sorter and assure that sorted cells fall in the middle of the well. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S11 -->
11. Proceed with single-cell sorting of KO or KI cells using a minimum flow rate to maximize viability and purity. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S12 -->

### Transfection of hiPSCs with CRISPR-Cas9 tools

1. Seed hiPSCs for cell transfection. Expand hiPSCs in culture to obtain the required number of cells for KO or KI generation (refer to 'transfection reaction mixes' table in materials section). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S01 -->
2. Replace hiPSC culturing medium with hiPSC single-cell medium. Aspirate the existing medium, add 1.5 mL of hiPSC single-cell medium per well, and incubate for at least 1 h at 37°C in a humidified atmosphere of 5% CO2 and 4% O2. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S02 -->
3. Coat each well of a 6-well plate with 1 mL Matrigel solution for one hour as described previously. Aspirate the Matrigel solution and add 1.5 mL of hiPSC single-cell medium per well. Prepare the total number of wells needed based on the 'transfection reaction mixes' table. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S03 -->
4. Dissociate hiPSCs into a single-cell suspension. Incubate hiPSCs with GCDR for 20-30 min to ensure complete dissociation into single cells. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S04 -->
5. Gently pipet the dissociated hiPSCs using 1 mL of hiPSC single-cell medium per well to create a uniform suspension. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S05 -->
6. Pool the dissociated cells from 3 to 5 wells by transferring the cell suspensions into a single 15 mL Falcon tube. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S06 -->
7. Take 50 µL of the cell suspension and proceed to cell counting using a Malassez counting chamber. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S07 -->
8. After counting, collect the volume of cell suspension containing 1 x 10^6 cells for one transfection reaction. Transfer this volume into a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube. Prepare the total number of tubes needed according to the 'transfection reaction mixes' table. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S08 -->
9. Centrifuge the 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes at 100 x g for 5 min at 21°C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S09 -->
10. Discard the cell supernatant carefully. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S10 -->
11. Transfect hiPSCs with CRISPR-Cas9 RNP complex and donor DNA. Add 100 µL of the transfection reaction mix (containing the prepared RNP and/or donor DNA) per transfection reaction to each cell pellet. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S11 -->
12. Add CRISPR-Cas9 tools (crRNA, tracrRNA, Cas9, donor DNA) according to the 'transfection reaction mixes' table. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S12 -->
13. Gently pipet up and down until the cell pellet is completely mixed with the CRISPR-Cas9 tools. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S13 -->
14. Transfer the cell suspension into a 100 µL Nucleocuvette vessel. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S14 -->
15. Proceed immediately with nucleofection using Program CA-137 on a 4D-Nucleofector Core Unit. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S15 -->
16. Remove transfected cells from the nucleocuvette using the pipette provided by the nucleofection kit. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S16 -->
17. Seed the transfected cells drop-by-drop into one Matrigel-pre-coated well of a 6-well plate containing 1.5 mL of hiPSC single-cell medium. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S17 -->
18. Incubate the plate for 24 h at 37°C in a humidified atmosphere under hypoxic conditions (4% O2). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S18 -->

### 48 h post transfection

#### Branch: Single cell FACS sorting may be performed 48 h post transfection

1. Optional: Single-cell FACS sorting may be performed 48 h post-transfection. If proceeding with this option, replace hiPSC single-cell medium with standard hiPSC culturing medium the day after transfection. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T5-S01 -->

### hiPSCs single-cell sorting

1. Prepare 96-well cell culture plates for hiPSC single-cell sorting. Coat four 96-well plates with 50 µL of Matrigel solution per well. Incubate at 37°C for at least one hour. Remove Matrigel by aspiration and add 100 µL of hiPSC single-cell medium per well. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T6-S01 -->
2. Perform single-cell dissociation of transfected hiPSCs. Incubate hiPSCs with GCDR for 20-30 min. Add 1 mL of hiPSC single-cell medium and gently pipet. Transfer dissociated hiPSCs into a 15 mL tube. Centrifuge at 100 x g for 5 min at 4°C. Discard supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet with 500 µL of hiPSC single-cell medium. Place the 15 mL tube on ice until single-cell FACS sorting. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T6-S02 -->
3. Filter the cell suspension through a 70 µm nylon mesh cell strainer. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T6-S03 -->
4. Transfer the filtered cell suspension into a 5 mL sterile polypropylene tube suitable for cytometry. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T6-S04 -->
5. Perform calibration and adjust gates as described in the 'FACS sorter set-up' section. Analyze the transfected cells to sort them. Insert the four 96-well plates into the cytometer one at a time and sort one cell per well. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T6-S05 -->
6. Incubate the 96-well plates immediately at 37°C in a humidified atmosphere under hypoxic conditions (4% O2). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T6-S06 -->

### ten days

1. Keep hiPSC clones in culture for a total of ten days. Change the medium with 100 µL fresh medium every two days. Use hiPSC single-cell medium during the first week after sorting, then switch to hiPSC culturing medium for the last 3 days. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T7-S01 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL: Keep hiPSC clones for two to three days after single-cell sorting without changing media to allow initial recovery. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T7-S02 -->

### two to three days after duplication

#### Branch: Large colonies

1. If hiPSC clones form large colonies, dissociate and duplicate them into two wells of two separate 96-well cell culture plates. Coat 96-well plates with 50 µL of 0.05 mg/mL Matrigel per well and incubate at 37°C for one hour (prepare 2 new plates for each original plate of clones). Remove Matrigel and fill each well with 100 µL of hiPSC single-cell medium. Wash clones twice with 100 µL DPBS wo Ca2+/Mg2+. Dissociate using 100 µL GCDR per well for 5-10 min. Remove GCDR by aspiration as soon as cells start to dissociate. Detach cells by pipetting up and down with 100 µL hiPSC single-cell medium. Transfer 50 µL of cell suspension into two wells of two distinct 96-well plates. Incubate at 37°C in humidified atmosphere under hypoxia (4% O2) for 24 h. Replace medium with 100 µL hiPSC culturing medium every two days. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T8-S01 -->

### Genotyping preparation

1. Lyse cells from one 96-well plate for genotyping when confluent. Wash wells twice with 100 µL DPBS wo Ca2+/Mg2+. Add 50 µL of QuickExtract DNA extraction solution to a confluent well. Scrape cells at the bottom of the well using a pipette tip. Seal the 96-well plate with parafilm and freeze at -20°C for further DNA extraction. Proceed with DNA extraction. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T9-S01 -->
2. Freeze cells of the second 96-well plate for future amplification of genetically-engineered clones of interest. Wash wells twice with 100 µL DPBS wo Ca2+/Mg2+ per well. Dissociate hiPSC clones in 100 µL GCDR per well for 5-10 min. Remove GCDR by aspiration before cells completely detach. Detach cells by pipetting up and down with 100 µL of CryoStor CS10 cryopreservation medium. Seal the 96-well plate with parafilm and quickly transfer it to an -80°C freezer. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T9-S02 -->

### 1 h

#### Branch: DNA extraction for genotyping of hiPSCs clones

1. Perform DNA extraction for genotyping. Thaw the 96-well plate prepared for genotyping on ice. Transfer DNA cell extracts into a 96-well PCR plate using a multichannel pipette. Proceed with DNA extraction in a thermocycler using the following program: 65°C for 15 min, 68°C for 15 min, and 98°C for 10 min. Proceed directly to genotyping as described in Bray et al. (2022) and Canac et al. (2022). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T10-S01 -->

### 1-2 weeks

#### Branch: Thawing and ampliﬁcation of genetically modiﬁed hiPSCs clones

1. Amplify genetically-modified hiPSC clones of interest after genotyping. Determine the position of the clones of interest in the 96-well plate. For one clone to be amplified, coat a well of a 12-well microplate with 0.5 mL of Matrigel solution (0.05 mg/mL) for at least one hour. Aspirate Matrigel and fill the well with 1 mL of hiPSC single-cell medium. Thaw the 96-well plate prepared for clonal amplification by transferring it directly from the -80°C freezer to a 37°C incubator. Transfer the 100 µL thawed cell suspension directly into the 12-well plate. Incubate at 37°C in humidified atmosphere under hypoxia (4% O2) for 24 h. Replace hiPSC single-cell medium with hiPSC culturing medium. Refresh medium every two days and amplify cells for banking. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T11-S01 -->

### 2 h

1. Prepare 96-well cell culture plates for hiPSC single-cell sorting. [1] <!-- protocol-step:S70 -->
2. Coat four 96-well cell culture plates with 50 µL of Matrigel solution per well. [1] <!-- protocol-step:S71 -->
3. Incubate the 96-well plates at 37°C for at least one hour. [1] <!-- protocol-step:S72 -->
4. Remove Matrigel solution by aspiration and then add 100 µL of hiPSC single-cell medium per well. [1] <!-- protocol-step:S73 -->
5. Perform single-cell dissociation of transfected hiPSCs. [1] <!-- protocol-step:S74 -->
6. Dissociate transfected hiPSCs into single cells by incubating with GCDR for 20-30 min. [1] <!-- protocol-step:S75 -->
7. Add 1 mL of hiPSC single-cell medium and gently pipet the dissociated hiPSCs. [1] <!-- protocol-step:S76 -->
8. Transfer dissociated hiPSCs into a 15 mL tube. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S08 -->
9. Centrifuge the dissociated hiPSCs at 100 x g for 5 min at 4°C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S09 -->
10. Discard the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet with 500 µL of hiPSC single-cell medium. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S10 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Place the 15 mL tube on ice until single-cell FACS sorting. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S11 -->
11. Perform calibration and adjust gates as described in the FACS sorter set-up section. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S14 -->
12. Analyze the transfected cells to sort them and proceed with single-cell sorting. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S15 -->
13. Insert the four 96-well plates into the cytometer one at a time and sort one cell per well. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S16 -->

### 10-15 days

1. 8. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T1-S01 -->
